title: Bounded work
tagline: Limit concurrent batch work to two jobs.
problem: A batch of jobs should not turn into an unbounded pile of work.
notes: Reduced the canonical parallel_map example to four inputs and a limit of two. This verifies results and ordering, not a speedup.
post: I want batch work to have a ceiling. This Kujo example maps four inputs with a concurrency limit of two, then awaits the results. Small enough to read at a glance. No speedup claim, just an explicit limit.

title: Read it twice
tagline: Await the same task result more than once.
problem: Reading a completed task once should not consume its result.
notes: Extracted the reusable-completion contract into a standalone example. Both waits return 21; cancelling the completed task returns false.
post: A task result should not disappear because something already waited for it. This Kujo example awaits the same task twice and gets the same value. Cancelling it after completion returns false. Useful behavior to make explicit.

title: Stop a task
problem: A background task needs a deliberate stop path.
notes: Reduced the lifecycle cancellation contract. The shared started flag prevents a start/cancel race. Cancellation is cooperative; this does not promise interruption of arbitrary blocking native calls.
post: Background work needs a stop path. This Kujo example waits until a task starts, cancels it, and handles the rejected await. It demonstrates cooperative cancellation, not a magic undo button for side effects.

title: Stable JSON
tagline: Stable JSON, even when key order changes.
problem: Dictionary insertion order creates noisy diffs and unstable machine output.
notes: Reduced the canonical HLP-015 example to nested key ordering and equality.
post: Noisy JSON diffs waste review time. Kujo serializes these nested dictionaries identically even though the keys were inserted in a different order. Tiny example, useful property for files that people and tools both read.

title: Read the exit
tagline: Read exit status without parsing text.
problem: Shell text alone does not tell an agent whether a process timed out or failed.
notes: Adapted HLP-013 from rustc --version to a portable printf command. Checks success and exitcode, then prints structured output, timeout and truncation flags.
post: When an agent runs a command, I want more than a blob of terminal text. This Kujo example checks success and exit status, then reads stdout, timeout, and truncation fields directly. No parsing a status message.

title: Safer output
tagline: Redact secrets in print and JSON output.
problem: A debug print can accidentally disclose a credential.
notes: Reduced the canonical secret example; the dummy value is not a credential. Redaction is not encryption and explicit reveal remains possible.
post: A debug print should not casually dump a secret. Wrapping this dummy value with secret() makes Kujo redact it in both print and JSON output. This example checks those boundaries; it does not claim encryption.

title: Eval
tagline: Check a command and its manifest fixture.
problem: A successful command alone is not a complete release smoke check.
notes: Executed the unchanged canonical three-check release suite against its copied kennel.toml fixture. This checks a command, file existence, and file size; it does not evaluate model quality.
post: “It ran” is a weak handoff. This Eval example runs the canonical release smoke suite: a command succeeds, the manifest exists, and its size clears the check. The JSON results stay available for the next tool or reviewer.

title: Workcell
problem: Execution settings are hard to review when they are buried in launch commands.
notes: Executed validate and inspect --summary on the unchanged hello definition. No container was launched; Docker was unavailable. Network none and resource limits are resolved policy, not observed enforcement.
post: Before running agent work, I want to see the boundaries. Workcell resolves this hello definition into a compact policy summary: network off, read-only root, explicit limits. This card verifies preflight; it does not claim a container ran.

title: PackWrite
tagline: Offline pack checks. No model call.
problem: An incomplete agent pack can send the next session into guesswork.
notes: Executed validate and summary on the released golden-agent fixture with six phases. The fixture is a test input, not newly generated model output. No provider was called.
post: An agent handoff is only useful if the pieces are there. Here PackWrite validates an existing six-phase fixture and reports no missing files. This is the offline validation path, not a claim about a freshly generated plan.

title: RunLedger
tagline: Keep a run receipt after the chat ends.
problem: An agent session ends, and its run context disappears into chat history.
notes: Executed a scripted receipt lifecycle using provider local and model scripted-example. Pass is a supplied demonstration verdict. No token usage, costs, model invocation, or automated quality judgment is claimed.
post: I do not want run history trapped in chat. This RunLedger example starts a local receipt, finishes it, writes a report, and checks the ledger. The verdict is supplied by the caller. Token usage and costs stay unset.

title: Lens
tagline: Check desktop and mobile; keep evidence.
problem: A page can look fine at one size and still have console or layout problems.
notes: Executed a local dashboard fixture with desktop/mobile screenshots, accessibility and link checks. Adapted the canonical spec by removing unsupported not_exists. No accessibility certification or production-site coverage is claimed.
post: “Looks fine here” is not much evidence. Lens checked this local dashboard at desktop and mobile sizes, applied the supported spec assertions, and saved screenshots plus reports. Useful handoff material without an LLM judging the page.

title: ShipCheck
problem: A release checklist is easy to forget when shipping gets busy.
notes: Executed gate --format json against the pinned ShipCheck release checkout. This checks repository readiness signals, not test execution, artifact integrity, or release certification.
post: Release prep should not depend on remembering every file. ShipCheck gates this pinned repo checkout on its readiness checks and returns JSON plus an exit code. It checks release signals; it does not run the project tests for you.
